grades.quote: Path name lookup involves a succession of calls to dirlookup, one for each path component. namei (5590) evaluates path and returns the corresponding inode.
grades.reason: Explains the name layer. Path components are resolved through directory lookups (dirlookup) to an inode, and namei returns the inode. This covers the directory-entry-to-inode relationship. It does not address file descriptors or contrast the three layers.
This is a list of chapter exercises. It has no substantive explanation of inodes, directory entries or file descriptors. The questions only touch on related topics.

grades.quote: A file descriptor, on the other hand, provides no information about the file’s name or location; it is just a featureless integer.
grades.reason: Contrasts pathnames (the name layer) with file descriptors (an opaque per-process handle that carries no name or location information). It does not cover inodes or directory entries directly.

grades.quote: Each open file is represented by a struct file (4200), which is a wrapper around either an inode or a pipe, plus an I/O offset.
grades.reason: Describes the file descriptor layer. Per-process descriptors point to open-file structures that wrap an inode and add an I/O offset. This separates the descriptor and open-file layer from the underlying inode. It does not discuss directory entries.
